verses.text: The LORD gave this message to Jonah son of Amittai:
"Get up and go to the great city of Nineveh. Preach against it, because I have seen how wicked its people are."

But Jonah got up and ran away from the LORD. He headed for Tarshish. He went down to the port of Joppa, where he found a ship leaving for Tarshish. He paid the fare and went on board, to sail with the crew to Tarshish, away from the LORD.
But the LORD sent a strong wind over the sea, and a violent storm came up. The storm was so bad that the ship was about to break apart.

The sailors were terrified, and each one cried out to his own god. They threw the cargo into the sea to make the ship lighter. But Jonah had gone below deck, where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
The captain went to him and said, "How can you sleep? Get up and call on your god! Maybe your god will notice us, and we will not die."
Then the sailors said to each other, "Come, let us throw dice to find out who is to blame for this disaster." So they threw dice, and Jonah was chosen.
So they asked him, "Tell us, who is to blame for this disaster? What do you do for a living? Where do you come from? What is your country? What people do you belong to?"
He answered, "I am a Hebrew. I worship the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."
This terrified the sailors, and they said to him, "What have you done?" They knew he was running away from the LORD, because he had told them so.
The sea was getting rougher and rougher. So they asked him, "What should we do to you to make the sea calm down for us?"
He told them, "Pick me up and throw me into the sea, and it will become calm. I know it is my fault that this terrible storm has come on you."
But the men rowed hard to try to get back to land. They could not, because the sea grew even wilder against them.
Then they cried out to the LORD, "Please, LORD, please do not let us die for taking this man's life. Do not hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. For you, LORD, have done what you wanted."
Then they picked Jonah up and threw him into the sea, and the raging sea grew calm.
At this the men greatly feared the LORD. They offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made promises to him.
The LORD sent a huge fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
